title: Tobit's journey (Tobit 1–6)
hookLine: a blind father, a son on a journey, a dog, and a stranger who turns out to be the angel Raphael

lines: AN OLD MAN WHO BURIES THE DEAD.
TWO PRAYERS ON THE SAME DAY.
cards: Tobit is an old Israelite in exile in Nineveh, with a dangerous habit. When his people are killed and their bodies thrown out unburied, he goes out at night and buries them, even after the king's men come looking for him.

One evening, worn out from burying, he lies down by a wall and falls asleep, and droppings from a nest above fall into his open eyes. He goes blind. He's poor now, quarrels with his wife Anna, and prays to die.
And on the very same day, far away in Media, a young woman named Sara is praying the same prayer.

teach.h: A SON SENT EAST FOR THE MONEY.
teach.b: The book tells us both prayers were heard at once, and that God sent the angel Raphael to help them both.
Tobit remembers money he once left in trust with a kinsman, Gabelus, in a city in Media, far to the east, and sends his son Tobias to fetch it.

Tobias doesn't know the road, so he goes out to find a guide, and there's a young man standing there, ready, as if he'd been waiting. He says his name is Azarias, a relative, and he knows the way. He's Raphael.
Nobody in the story finds out until the very end.
And the story adds a lovely detail: the dog went with them. One of the only good dogs in the whole Bible, trotting behind an angel and a boy.
The first night they reach the river Tigris, and when Tobias goes down to wash his feet, a huge fish leaps out at him. The guide says: take hold of it, and drag it to land.
Keep its heart, its gall and its liver; they'll be needed for medicine.
Raphael is a Hebrew name, and it means God heals.
That's the shape of the whole book: a blind father, a grieving young woman, a son sent on an errand, and healing walking beside them unrecognized.
Catholics keep Raphael as a patron of travelers and of the sick, with his feast on the twenty-ninth of September, alongside Michael and Gabriel.

how: Catholics honor Saint Raphael with Michael and Gabriel on September 29 and ask his prayers for travelers, the sick, and those seeking a spouse; the Book of Tobit is read at weekday Mass.

o: a son's road trip guided by an angel in disguise
an old man's pilgrimage back to Jerusalem
a prophet's flight by ship from God's call

games.q: on the road from Nineveh — tap the pairs.

s: Tobias knows from the start that his guide is an angel
the guide calls himself Azarias. nobody in the story learns he is Raphael until the end.
Tobit went blind while sleeping under a nest
worn out from burying the dead, he lay down by a wall, and droppings fell into his eyes.
in the Douay's version, a dog goes along on the journey
the Latin text says the dog followed them.

games.q: you're Tobias, washing your feet in the Tigris on the first night, when a huge fish leaps out at you. your guide shouts. what does he tell you?
o: take hold of it and drag it to land.
jump into the river after it.
games.why: take hold of it, and keep its heart, gall and liver. they'll be needed for healing later in the story.

practice: Think of someone on a road right now: a long drive, a new city, or a harder journey through an illness or a loss. Picture someone walking beside them whom they might not recognize.
Catholics often ask Raphael to pray for travelers, the way they'd ask a friend; if you pray, ask him to walk with this person today, and if you don't, just hold them in mind, arriving safely.

wordCard.voice: Tobit's journey. A blind father, his son Tobias on the road, a faithful dog, and a guide who was the angel Raphael, whose name means God heals. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: Raphael, God heals, from rapha, to heal, and El, God.

carryVoice: Your line: raphael walks with you. And the dog went too. Day four hundred thirty-seven, done.
